brief.topic: The Uneven Rings Left by a Moving Sound

s01: A moving sound leaves an uneven pattern behind.
The rings crowd together in front and open out behind.
Watch the places where each ring began.
Each pulse starts at the source, then spreads through still air.
The old rings do not follow the moving source.
The next pulse begins a little farther forward.
Let us hold that pattern still.
In one beat, the wave travels this far.
The source travels part of that distance too.
Ahead, subtract the distance moved by the source.
Behind, add it instead.
That creates two different gaps from one steady rhythm.
When we let the pattern move, closely spaced waves arrive more often.
A listener ahead hears a higher pitch.
A listener behind hears a lower one.
The source itself has not changed its note.
Compare with a source at rest.
Now each new ring begins at the same point.
The gaps match in every direction.
This is an ideal drawing of sound in still air, with a source slower than sound.
Light needs a different formula.
The surprise is in the spacing: movement reshapes the rhythm that reaches us.

scenes.narration:
A moving sound leaves an uneven pattern behind. The rings crowd together in front and open out behind. Watch the places where each ring began.

Each pulse starts at the source, then spreads through still air. The old rings do not follow the moving source. The next pulse begins a little farther forward. Let us hold that pattern still.

In one beat, the wave travels this far. The source travels part of that distance too. Ahead, subtract the distance moved by the source. Behind, add it instead. That creates two different gaps from one steady rhythm.

When we let the pattern move, closely spaced waves arrive more often. A listener ahead hears a higher pitch. A listener behind hears a lower one. The source itself has not changed its note.

Compare with a source at rest. Now each new ring begins at the same point. The gaps match in every direction. This is an ideal drawing of sound in still air, with a source slower than sound. Light needs a different formula. The surprise is in the spacing: movement reshapes the rhythm that reaches us.
